finding_origin: MEGA_PLAN_SYNC_HARDENING_v3 §3.4. Risque opérationnel: aucune métrique business ne couvre la sync POS↔Borne↔KDS. Quand un opérateur dit "le KDS rame", on n'a pas de chiffres pour décider si c'est WS down, queue saturée, ou polling fallback. Sans métriques: pas de SLO mesurable, pas de pager rule actionnable, pas de capacité de root-cause sans accès SSH live.

scope_files_to_create: database/migrations/2026_04_23_220000_create_sync_metrics_table.php — Table `sync_metrics`: id (bigIncrements), metric_type (string 64, indexed), branch_id (unsignedBigInteger nullable, indexed), value (bigInteger; suit la sémantique du metric: latence ms / count 1 / interval ms), correlation_id (char 36 nullable), labels (json nullable; clés-valeurs supplémentaires {event_type:..., from:..., to:...}), occurred_at (dateTime(3), indexed). Indexes: (metric_type, occurred_at) pour les rollups, (branch_id, occurred_at) pour les vues par branche. Pas d'index unique. Garder léger: pas de FK pour ne pas bloquer les écritures à haut débit.

app/Services/Observability/SyncMetricsRecorder.php — Service singleton (binding via AppServiceProvider — voir non_negotiable_constraints). Methods: (a) recordEventDispatched(string $eventType, ?int $branchId, int $latencyMs, ?string $correlationId = null): void — insert metric_type='outbox.dispatch_latency_ms', value=$latencyMs, labels={event_type}; (b) recordWebSocketAuthFailure(?int $branchId, ?string $correlationId = null): void — insert metric_type='ws.auth_failure', value=1; (c) recordKdsSyncFallback(?int $branchId, int $intervalMs, ?string $reason = null, ?string $correlationId = null): void — insert metric_type='kds.sync_fallback_interval_ms', value=$intervalMs, labels={reason}; (d) recordClientMetric(string $metricType, ?int $branchId, int $value, array $labels, ?string $correlationId = null): void — generic ingest from frontend batcher; whitelist metricType against ALLOWED_CLIENT_METRICS const (cf. backend_contract). Toutes les insertions utilisent DB::table('sync_metrics')->insert([...]) (pas Eloquent — performance-first, écritures fire-and-forget). occurred_at = now() avec milliseconds. Le service NE doit JAMAIS lever d'exception qui propage: try/catch interne avec Log::warning sur erreur de persistance + return early — la télémétrie ne doit JAMAIS casser un flux métier (invariant_observability_non_blocking).

app/Http/Controllers/Admin/Observability/SyncOverviewController.php — Controller. Method index(Request $request): JsonResponse — query param `branch_id` (optionnel; null = toutes branches autorisées par le user), `since` (ISO8601 default = -1h). Réponse: { generated_at, since, branch_id, summary: { outbox_dispatch_latency_ms_p50, outbox_dispatch_latency_ms_p95, outbox_dispatch_latency_ms_p99, outbox_events_count, ws_auth_failures_count, kds_fallback_count, kds_fallback_interval_ms_p50 }, by_event_type: [{event_type, count, latency_p95_ms}], recent_failures: [{...top 10 failures from domain_events where last_error is not null + dispatched_at is null}] }. Percentile calculation: sort en mémoire (rolling window <=1h, ~10k rows max → OK). Method clientMetrics(Request $request): JsonResponse — POST body { metrics: [{type, value, labels?, occurred_at}] }, max 200 metrics par batch (HTTP 413 sinon), valide avec FormRequest, récupère branch_id depuis auth()->user(), append correlation_id depuis request header, déclenche SyncMetricsRecorder::recordClientMetric() pour chaque entrée. Retourne 202 Accepted + { received: <count> }.

app/Http/Requests/Admin/Observability/StoreClientMetricsRequest.php — FormRequest. Rules: 'metrics' => ['required','array','max:200']; 'metrics.*.type' => ['required','string','in:ws.connect_latency_ms,ws.disconnect_event,ws.reconnect_storm,kds.sync_fallback_interval_ms'] (whitelist stricte = ALLOWED_CLIENT_METRICS); 'metrics.*.value' => ['required','integer','min:0','max:600000']; 'metrics.*.labels' => ['sometimes','array']; 'metrics.*.occurred_at' => ['required','date']. authorize() → return $this->user() !== null.

resources/js/services/MetricsBatcher.js — ES module factory `createMetricsBatcher({ wsService, kdsSyncService, endpoint, fetcher, intervalMs = 60_000, maxBatch = 200 })`. Comportements: (a) maintient un buffer in-memory bornée à 200 entrées; (b) écoute wsService.on('reconnect_storm', payload => buffer.push({type:'ws.reconnect_storm', value: payload.delay_ms, labels:{attempts_in_window}, occurred_at: new Date().toISOString()})); (c) écoute wsService.on('state_change', ({previous,current}) => { if previous==='CONNECTED' && current!=='CONNECTED') buffer.push(disconnect_event)}); (d) écoute kdsSyncService.on('state_change', ({from,to,reason}) => buffer.push(kds.sync_fallback_interval_ms with current cadence)); (e) toutes les intervalMs (60s par défaut), si buffer non vide, POST à endpoint via fetcher (default global fetch) avec body {metrics: buffer.splice(0,maxBatch)} et header X-Correlation-ID lu depuis localStorage ou via window.__correlationId si dispo; (f) graceful degradation: erreur réseau / 4xx / 5xx → log console.warn une seule fois (warned flag), buffer reste, retry au prochain tick; (g) start() / stop() / destroy() pour lifecycle; (h) return public API: { start, stop, destroy, getBufferSize, _flushNow (test helper) }. Pas de mutation globale, pas de import direct de WebSocketService — injecté en factory.

backend_contract.metric_type_naming_convention: snake_case + dotted namespace: `outbox.dispatch_latency_ms`, `ws.auth_failure`, `ws.connect_latency_ms`, `ws.disconnect_event`, `ws.reconnect_storm`, `kds.sync_fallback_interval_ms`. Future metrics MUST follow this scheme to keep dashboards filterable.
backend_contract.ALLOWED_CLIENT_METRICS_whitelist: Strict whitelist enforced by FormRequest AND by SyncMetricsRecorder::recordClientMetric(). Any unknown type → reject silently with Log::warning. Reasoning: prevent untrusted clients from polluting the metrics table with arbitrary keys.
backend_contract.value_semantic_per_metric_type: outbox.dispatch_latency_ms = milliseconds; ws.auth_failure = always 1 (count); ws.connect_latency_ms = milliseconds; ws.disconnect_event = always 1 (count); ws.reconnect_storm = delay_ms (the breaker delay); kds.sync_fallback_interval_ms = current cadence in ms.
backend_contract.non_blocking_telemetry_invariant: SyncMetricsRecorder MUST swallow ALL exceptions internally (DB down, table missing, etc.) and only Log::warning. The CALLER MUST be able to fire-and-forget without a try/catch. Test (e) in SyncMetricsRecorderTest enforces this.
backend_contract.percentile_calculation: In-memory sort via array_values(sort + index lookup). For N <= 50_000 (1h rolling window cap), this is O(N log N) and runs in <100ms. If N grows, switch to a streaming digest (t-digest) — explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for NEW-04.
backend_contract.correlation_id_propagation: Recorder reads correlation_id from arg if provided (jobs path). Otherwise reads from `request()->header('X-Correlation-ID')` if a request is in scope (HTTP path). Otherwise null. Stored in sync_metrics.correlation_id for cross-system tracing.
backend_contract.client_metrics_endpoint_throttling: Apply throttle:60,1 (60 requests/min per user) on POST /api/admin/observability/client-metrics. The MetricsBatcher posts every 60s by default → headroom for retries. Document in route declaration.
